title: Continuous integration that blocks unapproved public APIs
hook: Every public type in a shared library is a contract. Continuous integration (CI) can diff public API surface between builds and fail pull requests that add breaking changes without approval — the same discipline product teams use before publishing NuGet packages.

blocks.text: Public API analyzers compare the exported surface of an assembly between a baseline and the current build. Adding a method might be compatible; removing or changing signature is breaking. Tools like Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.PublicApiAnalyzers, ApiCompat, or custom scripts on reflection output gate merges. Pair with semantic versioning and InternalsVisibleTo so experiments stay internal until ready.

entries.plainDefinition: All public and protected types and members visible to consumers of an assembly.
entries.example: public class OrderService { public Task Submit() }

entries.plainDefinition: Tooling that compares two builds for API compatibility.
entries.example: CI fails if a public method is removed.

entries.plainDefinition: Change that forces consumers to recompile or breaks at runtime.
entries.example: Renaming a public method or changing parameter types.

blocks.text: A domain package referenced by three microservices cannot casually rename public DTOs. CI guards catch accidental public exposure of internal types. Interviewers ask how you prevent library semver violations — answer with access modifiers, review radar, and automated API diff in pull request checks.

blocks.title: Default to internal
blocks.body: Make new types internal until you deliberately expose them. Public is a publishing decision.

snippet.label: PublicApiAnalyzers package
snippet.explanation: Adds RS0016 and related diagnostics when public API changes without updating Shipped/Unshipped txt files.

snippet.label: Keep experiments internal
snippet.explanation: Internal engine can change freely. Public facade is the stable contract CI watches.

snippet.label: CI api compat check
snippet.code:
dotnet build -c Release
# ApiCompat or custom tool:
dotnet-apicompat --baseline artifacts/MyLib.1.0.0.dll --current bin/Release/net10.0/MyLib.dll
snippet.explanation: Pipeline step blocks merge when binary compatibility breaks without approval.

snippet.label: PublicApiAnalyzers shipped baseline
snippet.code:
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.PublicApiAnalyzers" Version="*" PrivateAssets="All" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
<!-- PublicAPI.Shipped.txt and PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt in repo -->
snippet.explanation: Analyzers diff public surface against checked-in baseline files — CI fails on unapproved API changes.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Making everything public for convenience. Forgetting to update PublicAPI files so CI always fails. Changing public record positional parameter order — breaking for callers.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: PublicApiAnalyzers and Microsoft.DotNet.ApiCompat.Tooling compare current public surface to Shipped.txt baseline in CI — failed PR means semver violation. internal by default keeps experiments out of the contract. Adding a public method is usually additive (minor bump); removing or changing signatures is major. Pair with nullable warnings as errors in library csproj. For NuGet consumers, binding redirects and package validation catch accidental breaks before publish.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Making helpers public 'for tests' instead of InternalsVisibleTo. Not knowing positional record parameter reorder breaks binary compatibility. Skipping baseline update and disabling the analyzer instead of intentional major bump. Claiming semver is only package.json — .NET public API is the assembly contract.

interviewTakeaways: Public API is a published contract — default to internal and guard surface with PublicApiAnalyzers or ApiCompat in CI.
Breaking changes require major semver and baseline update; additive members are usually safe minor changes.
In production, library CI should fail PRs that change Shipped.txt without reviewer approval and version bump.
60s: Public API is contract. internal by default. CI diffs against baseline. Major for removals and signature breaks. InternalsVisibleTo for tests, not public helpers.
Follow-up: is adding a default parameter value a breaking change?
commonPitfalls: Public types that should be internal gets you rejected — pollutes contract and blocks refactoring.
Changing positional record parameter order without major bump.
Strong answer: 'PublicApiAnalyzers in CI. internal default. Facade pattern for stable surface. Major bump plus baseline update for breaks.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: api-extractor rolls up .d.ts and detects breaking changes in exported types — parallel to .NET PublicApiAnalyzers.
The exports map defines the public npm surface like assembly public types — changing export paths is a breaking change for consumers.
